name: Michael J. Widener
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Michael J. Widener, Professor of Geography & Planning at the University of Toronto and member of the SAUSy Lab, researching health geography, the built environment and mobility.
bio: Michael is a quantitative health geographer with interests in food retail, mobility, access to health care, and urban environments.

name: Steven Farber
profileRole: Professor, Transportation geography and urban mobility
department: Department of Human Geography, University of Toronto Scarborough
description: Steven Farber, Professor of Human Geography at the University of Toronto Scarborough and member of the SAUSy Lab, researching transportation equity and accessibility.
bio: Steven is a Professor of Human Geography at the University of Toronto Scarborough, specializing in transportation geography and urban mobility.

Steven's research examines the relationships between transportation systems, social equity, accessibility, and participation in everyday life, with a particular focus on transport poverty and the ways mobility shapes social and economic opportunities. A central interest is how transportation and land-use policies can contribute to more equitable, sustainable, and accessible cities.

Steven also leads large interdisciplinary research partnerships that connect academic research with transportation planning and public policy, including the Mobilizing Justice partnership and the University of Toronto Mobility Network.

name: Ignacio Tiznado Aitken
profileRole: Assistant Professor, Transport geography and planning
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Ignacio Tiznado Aitken, Assistant Professor of Geography & Planning at the University of Toronto and member of the SAUSy Lab, researching transport geography, transport planning and transport inequalities.
bio: Ignacio is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Geography and Planning at the University of Toronto and Associate Director of the Mobilizing Justice project. Ignacio holds a PhD in Transportation Engineering from the Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile, was a postgraduate researcher at the Institute for Transport Studies at the University of Leeds (2018–2019), worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the Center for Sustainable Urban Development (2020–2021), and served as research coordinator of the Suburban Mobilities Cluster (2021–2023).

Using multi-sourced data and spatial, mixed (quantitative and qualitative) methods, Ignacio's research covers a wide range of topics in transport and land use planning in urban and suburban areas, particularly: (i) geospatial analytics of transport systems, especially public transport, considering system performance, travel behaviour and user experiences; (ii) transport equity and the distribution of transport-related benefits and burdens across space for different population groups; and (iii) sustainable transport and urban space allocation policies that consider new mobility trends such as micromobility.

name: Christopher D. Higgins
department: Department of Human Geography, University of Toronto Scarborough
description: Christopher D. Higgins, Associate Professor of Human Geography at the University of Toronto Scarborough and member of the SAUSy Lab, researching accessibility, urban form and spatial analysis.
bio: Christopher is a quantitative geographer whose research focuses on the relationship between form and function in cities.

Using the tools and methods of GIS and geographic data science, Christopher's work captures and models the physical form and infrastructure of the city, its urban networks and the flows of people, goods, and information they facilitate, and the use of the city as an area or volume for engaging in activities. By providing a window into how the dynamic state of the city impacts and is impacted by social, environmental, and economic processes, this work seeks to better inform policy and planning interventions and promote more sustainable urban outcomes.

name: Andrei Botescu
profileRole: MScPl student, Transportation planning and infrastructure
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Andrei Botescu, MScPl student in transportation planning at the University of Toronto and member of the SAUSy Lab.
bio: Andrei is a Master of Science in Planning (MScPl) student at the University of Toronto, specializing in transportation planning and infrastructure. He previously completed an Honours Bachelor of Arts in Human Geography and French at UTSC.

His research interests focus on transportation planning and accessibility, and suburb-to-suburb transit, particularly how transportation networks and urban form influence mobility opportunities. As a researcher with Mobilizing Justice and SAUSy Lab, he worked with the National Survey of Transport Poverty to examine transportation experiences and inequalities across different populations and geographic contexts.
His methodological interests include quantitative data analysis, GIS, statistical modelling, and spatial analysis to better understand transportation disadvantage and accessibility.

name: Sandesh Bhandari
profileRole: MScPl student, Spatial statistics and Urban analytics
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Sandesh Bhandari is an MScPl student at the University of Toronto whose research focuses on spatial statistics, machine learning, and urban spatial analysis.
bio: Sandesh Bhandari is a Master of Science in Planning (MScPl) student at the University of Toronto, with an Honours Bachelor of Science.

His research interests focus on the application of spatial statistics and machine learning to urban environments, exploring how cities can be modeled and understood using geographic, remote sensing, and Earth systems data at fine spatial scales.
His current research examines urban heat exposure across transportation networks and housing intensification along Toronto’s major streets using geospatial analysis and machine learning.

name: Frédéric Cournoyer
profileRole: PhD student, Accessibility and transportation planning
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Frédéric Cournoyer, PhD student in geography at the University of Toronto and member of the SAUSy Lab, researching accessibility, transportation and urban planning.
bio: Frédéric is a PhD student in geography at the University of Toronto and holds a master’s degree in civil engineering from Polytechnique Montréal.

His research lies at the intersection of transportation and urban planning, with a particular focus on accessibility to destinations. In previous projects, he has examined the 15-minute city, park accessibility, and the integration of accessibility indicators into planning practice.

name: Nicole Hoh
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Nicole Hoh, MA student in Human Geography at the University of Toronto researching physical activity, active transportation and the built environment.
bio: Nicole graduated in 2025 with a Bachelor's degree in Kinesiology from the University of Toronto, where she focused on metabolic health and exercise physiology. She also worked as an Undergraduate research assistant in the BOSM Lab under Dr. Timothy Burkhart, exploring the impacts of iliopsoas tendon release surgery on patients with FAIS. She began her MA in Human Geography in 2025 and will graduate in 2027.

Her thesis focuses on using objective methods to examine the relationship between physical activity levels in university students and the modes of transport they use to travel between home and campus. Her study examines students' GPS commuting tracks, self-reported modes of transport, and accelerometer-measured physical activity over 48 hours to establish a complete activity and transportation profile for each participant. Her study hopes to find correlations between modes of transportation and physical activity levels, as well as with environmental active living scores and participant demographics. Nicole has also worked as a research assistant, performing GIS mapping of youth emotions and perceptions of healthy places in high-rise neighbourhoods.

name: Samantha Sharp
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Samantha Sharp, MA student at the University of Toronto researching health geography, time-use and caregiving.
bio: Hi! My name is Samantha and I'm an MA student in the Department of Geography and Planning at the University of Toronto. In 2026 I graduated from Western University with an HBA in GIS. As a graduate student, I am interested in research that uses spatial models and analysis to support questions related to health and time-use geographies. My thesis follows this interest, looking at the time-use sequencing and environments of caregivers in Canada.

name: Emma Cervinka
profileRole: PhD candidate, Youth geographies and active transportation
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Emma Cervinka, PhD candidate in the Department of Geography and Planning at the University of Toronto, researching youth geographies, active transportation and urban design.
bio: Emma Cervinka is a PhD candidate in the Department of Geography and Planning at the University of Toronto. She holds a Master of Urban Design from the University of British Columbia and a Bachelor of Landscape Architecture from the University of Guelph.

Her research interests include youth geographies, active transportation, urban design and planning policy, and mixed methods research. Her doctoral research focuses on how active travel contributes to young people’s sense of place and belonging in urban environments. She draws on her design education and professional experience to inform research on urban design that encourages active transportation, fosters community engagement and promotes public health.

name: Sana Riaz
profileRole: PhD candidate, Transport policy and electric mobility
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Sana Riaz, PhD candidate in planning at the University of Toronto and member of the SAUSy Lab, researching electric mobility, transport policy and just transitions.
bio: Sana Riaz is a PhD candidate in Planning at the University of Toronto. She holds a Master of Urban Planning from New York University and a Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Accounting and Finance from the Lahore University of Management Sciences, including a semester abroad at Stanford University.

Her research interests include transportation finance, transport policy for mode shift and emissions reduction, transit-oriented development, choice modelling, and spatial planning. She approaches this work through a lens of equity and justice. Her doctoral research examines consumer preferences for battery electric vehicles and e-bikes compared with conventional options, and how demand- and supply-side incentives shape uptake. Throughout, she pays attention to who benefits and who is left behind in the transition to electric mobility. She also assesses the related co-benefits for emissions and health, including physical activity.

She has work experience across intergovernmental organizations, academia, government, and the private sector, including the World Bank, the NYU Marron Institute, and the Urban Unit in Punjab, Pakistan.

name: Santiago Cardona-Urrea
profileRole: Postdoctoral researcher, Transport equity and accessibility
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Santiago Cardona-Urrea, postdoctoral researcher at the University of Toronto and member of the SAUSy Lab, researching accessibility and transport equity.
bio: Santiago is a transport and accessibility researcher with a PhD from Utrecht University. The main question driving this research is how transport can make cities and regions fairer.

The focus is on measures and indicators of transport equity, including how to calculate accessibility and the distribution of transport resources, with particular attention to sustainable modes such as walking, cycling, and public transport. Methodological expertise relies on spatial and quantitative analysis, including GIS, discrete choice models and factor analysis.

name: Chunjiang Li
profileRole: Postdoctoral fellow, Time geography and accessibility
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Chunjiang Li, postdoctoral fellow at the University of Toronto and member of the SAUSy Lab, researching time geography, space-time accessibility and food environments.
bio: Chunjiang Li is a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Geography and Planning at the University of Toronto. He holds a PhD in Human Geography from Peking University in China.

Chunjiang's research focuses on everyday activities from the time-geographic perspective. Research themes include: (1) physical-virtual hybridization of everyday activities; (2) space-time accessibility, particularly the 15-minute life circle (i.e., the Chinese version of the 15-minute city); and (3) food behaviour and food environment.

name: Ka Yiu (Benjamin) Ng
profileRole: Visiting PhD student, GIScience and spatial accessibility
department: Department of Geography, University of Hong Kong
description: Ka Yiu (Benjamin) Ng, PhD candidate at the University of Hong Kong and visiting student at the University of Toronto, researching GIScience, spatial accessibility and transport geography.
bio: Ka Yiu is a PhD candidate in the Department of Geography at the University of Hong Kong and a visiting student at the University of Toronto. Their research lies at the intersection of GIScience, transport geography, and health geography, with spatial access as a central theme, examining how the built environment, mobility, and accessibility shape everyday opportunities and wellbeing.

Methodologically, Ka Yiu draws on GIS, spatial analysis, accessibility modelling, transport data analytics, and mixed-method approaches to investigate human mobility and access. Current work extends these questions to pet-accompanied travel, exploring pet-friendly transport schemes and their implications for mobility practices. Ka Yiu is also interested in the ontology of errors in spatial accessibility modelling and its methodological consequences.

name: Brenn Anderson-Gregson
profileRole: PhD candidate, GIScience and transit accessibility
department: Department of Geography & Planning, University of Toronto
description: Brenn Anderson-Gregson, PhD candidate in planning at the University of Toronto and member of the SAUSy Lab, researching transit accessibility and mobility equity.
bio: Brenn is a PhD candidate in Planning at the University of Toronto. Their research sits at the intersection of GIScience, transportation planning, and mobility equity, with a central focus on measuring and evaluating transit accessibility.

They use computational and statistical methods to investigate whether objective accessibility metrics reflect real-world travel experiences, and to determine the most effective strategies for increasing and prioritizing transportation investment. Recent projects include testing foundation model embeddings for predicting accessibility across Canada’s largest census metropolitan areas, and analyzing nationally representative survey data to understand the gap between calculated transit access and people’s self-assessed transportation sufficiency.
Brenn is also interested in where bike paths, public transit lines, and brewery locations meet, examining the brewing landscape through interactive maps and creative cartography.
